properties.name: weakcrypto:config

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unsecured-JWT support in a JOSE library, changeable here: it is a shipped API a caller opts into by passing Secret::None; the header alg is deserialized from the token, so acceptance is caller-configured. No post-quantum migration target applies — the fix is 'use a real signature algorithm', and the D rating correctly reflects the missing integrity control, not a broken primitive.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256/384/512 JWS signing via ring, constant-time verification. Changeable here: a library can deprecate HS* in favour of asymmetric algorithms, but the quantum angle is minor (256-bit symmetric keys keep margin under Grover). The sites the collector found are serialization tests; the operations live in jwa.rs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Fuzz corpus material exercising the library's real HS256 paths: fuzz_signature_validation signs/verifies with hardcoded fuzz key "secret" (fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_signature_validation.rs:12); fuzz_decryption uses an all-zero 256-bit octet key with A256GCMKW+A256GCM (fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_decryption.rs:13). The HS256 implementation is live at src/jwa.rs:279-295 (ring hmac::HMAC_SHA256/384/512) with constant-time comparison at src/jwa.rs:364 (ring::constant_time::verify_slices_are_equal). Test dat

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-fixture RSA-2048 public key, no production value. Its sibling files in test/fixtures hold the matching PRIVATE key (reported as separate findings) — anyone triaging this object should check those. Key is classical RSA: Shor-vulnerable if it were ever used for real material, but as a fixture it documents the library's key format rather than protecting anything.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 in biscuit = key representation only: the live EllipticCurve::Curve25519 variant with serde rename "Ed25519" (src/jwk.rs:595-597) parses/serializes OKP JWKs and thumbprints them, but no Ed25519 signature is ever computed or verified. The implementation itself is compiled into ring 0.17 (ALG-683d5cd2). Availability + representation, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA P-256 JWS signing/verification via ring, exercised with test/fixtures/ecdsa_private_key.p8 (committed private key, reported separately). Changeable here: adding an ML-DSA (FIPS 204) or Ed25519 JWS algorithm is a library-level feature; today the ES* family is the only elliptic-curve signature path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring ~0.17.13 (Cargo.toml:26) is biscuit's sole crypto provider; its Ed25519 implementation ships in every build. Availability-in-shipped-library, no application call site — presence is the inventory question. ring 0.17 has no post-quantum algorithms; a future ML-DSA path means swapping or extending the provider. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is available in the shipped provider but performs nothing here. If ECDH-ES were ever implemented, X25519 (via OKP JWKs) is the curve it would use — at that point this becomes a live harvest-now-decrypt-later key-agreement surface → ML-KEM-768. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA P-384 (ES384) is the strongest elliptic-curve signature biscuit can actually perform; P-521 exists only as a parseable JWK curve value. Curve NIST secp384r1 meets CNSA 1.0 interim strength but is still classical — Shor-vulnerable, migration ML-DSA-65/87 on a schedule. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The only content-encryption algorithms biscuit implements are A128GCM/A256GCM (JWE 'enc'), plus the same primitive for CEK wrapping (A128GCMKW/A256GCMKW). Contrast: the enum also declares A128CBC-HS256/A192CBC-HS384/A256CBC-HS512 and A192GCM, but those hit Err(Error::UnsupportedOperation) — declared, refused, not shipped. Nonces are 96-bit from SystemRandom (random_aes_gcm_nonce, jwa.rs:793-798) or caller-supplied; tag length asserted 128-bit.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: A128GCM is the #[serde(default)] ContentEncryptionAlgorithm (jwa.rs:201-206): JWEs default to 128-bit AES-GCM unless the caller explicitly sets enc=A256GCM. That default is the changeable posture decision here — for long-lived ciphertexts, A256GCM is the conservative choice under Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live and reachable: JWK thumbprint (RFC 7638) hashes the key with SHA-256 via ring::digest::digest at src/jwk.rs:339 (jwk.algorithm.thumbprint(&crate::digest::SHA256)). SHA-2 is Grover-weakened only — quantum-safe class; CNSA 2.0 prefers a 384-bit digest. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live digest registry used by JWK thumbprints (src/jwk.rs:339); SHA-384/SHA-512 also back HS384/HS512 via ring hmac (src/jwa.rs:289-290). Meets CNSA 2.0 digest guidance. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: A256GCM is the strongest symmetric content encryption biscuit supports and is what its own JWE round-trip tests pair with A256GCMKW. No quantum concern beyond Grover, which 256-bit keys absorb.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring supplies every primitive biscuit performs: HMAC-SHA-2 (jwa.rs:279-295), AES-128/256-GCM content encryption and key wrap (jwa.rs:561-612/695-790), RSA PKCS1-v1_5 + PSS signatures 2048-8192 (jwa.rs:299-323/368-450), ECDSA P-256/P-384 (jwa.rs:325-342/384-385/437-438), SHA-2 digests, and SystemRandom CSPRNG; it also compiles in Ed25519 and X25519 (unused here). ring 0.17 has NO post-quantum algorithms — the PQ ceiling of everything downstream consumers do with biscuit is set by this provider. C

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The library owns no randomness of its own — every key and nonce originates from ring::rand::SystemRandom, so RNG posture is entirely delegated to ring and the OS. Nothing to migrate; the '?' rating is fine.
